newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW clears Bank Ochrony Srodowiska shares.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW clears Bank Ochrony Srodowiska shares.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) cleared Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS) shares for public trade, KPW said in a statement on Thursday.
BOS's president told a news conference the bank, which currently has 9.5 million shares, wanted to offer 1,200,000 shares in a public subscription scheduled for late October.
"The issue price will be set through a book-building at between 23 and 29 zlotys,"Jozef Koziol said.
The issue will be valid if investors subscribe for at least 600,000 shares.
He said he hoped BOS, which seeks main market listing, would enter the bourse in January 1997.
Koziol said 800,000 shares would be offered in a large investor tranche in October 21-25. In this tranche investors will be able to subscribe for more than 25,000 shares.
The small investor tranche of 400,000 shares in would be offered in October 21-31. In that tranche investors will be able to subscribe for between 10 and 25,000 shares.

He said the bank would decide in the next two or three weeks whether the issue would be underwritten and added that it had already received two offers from banks and several from outside the banking sector to underwrite the issue.
BOS, which specialises in funding environmental protection projects, had a net profit of 31.8 million zlotys in 1995 on 210.6 million zlotys in interest and other related revenues.
The bank's main shareholders are the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management, with 44.4 percent, the State Treasury, with 7.8 percent, and Ciech SA with 5.8 percent.
